User Story: As an operator, I can open the home, offer, and production workspaces from stable routes.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: / maps to home, /angebot maps to offer, /produktion maps to production; navigation renders route-specific content and masthead labels.

User Story: As an operator, I can see whether intake, offer, production, and export services are reachable.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Dashboard health state loads each service /health response and displays translated status/counts.
Primary Surface: UI home dashboard; API health endpoints

User Story: As an operator, I can see current counts for requests, specs, offers, plans, purchase lists, recipes, and audit events.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Dashboard aggregates list endpoints and formats counts with German labels.

User Story: As an operator, I can see the latest intake source, channel, filename, and ingestion warning context.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Latest request is selected by receivedAt and rendered with channel, filename, and ingestion warning summary when present.

User Story: As an operator, I can see recent audit activity as internal working evidence.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Audit entries are loaded from production audit endpoint and formatted with actor, action, timestamp, and summary.

User Story: As an operator, I can seed demo data for local rehearsal without using real customer data.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Seed action calls intake, offer, and production seed-demo endpoints and exposes success/failure feedback.
Primary Surface: UI home action; service seed endpoints

User Story: As an operator, I can set my display name and have mutating requests use it as the actor header.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Operator name persists in localStorage and API headers default to role-specific actor names when no custom name exists.

User Story: As an operator, I can see action success notices and errors in a common feedback surface.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: App stores notice/error state and renders it through the feedback shell after mutations.

Feature: Create offer draft from free text
User Story: As an offer operator, I can paste a customer request and create an offer draft.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: POST /v1/offers/from-text parses text into an event request, creates a draft, saves it, and logs audit metadata.

Feature: Create offer draft from structured event request
User Story: As an offer operator, I can create a draft from a structured EventRequest payload.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: POST /v1/offers/drafts validates EventRequest, creates and stores an OfferDraft, and logs readiness/variant count.

User Story: As an offer operator, supported event requests can use real curated package presets.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: selectCuratedPackage maps supported event/service combinations and min pax to fixture packages; unmatched or below-min-pax requests fall back.

User Story: As an offer operator, unsupported requests still receive a default offer draft.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: When no curated package matches, createOfferDraft is used and the meeting/coffee-break default path remains available.

User Story: As an offer operator, I can browse existing drafts and focus the active draft.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Dashboard loads offer drafts; offer route state filters/sorts and chooses selected or active draft.

Feature: Read customer-facing and internal offer text
User Story: As an offer operator, I can inspect customer-facing proposal text and internal review notes.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Focused draft renders summary, customer text, internal working text, open questions, and variants.

Feature: Promote offer variant to production spec
User Story: As an offer operator, I can hand an offer variant into an operative event specification.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: POST /v1/offers/drafts/:draftId/promote promotes requested or default variant into AcceptedEventSpec and logs audit.

User Story: As an offer operator, I can open a print-ready offer HTML export for a draft.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Export service requires offer operator, loads draft by id, returns text/html, and 404s unknown drafts.

User Story: As an offer operator, I can paste a local mini-pilot JSON result and see whether offer handoff is ready.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Mini-pilot panel parses ready/blocked JSON, shows reason/next step, persists local result, and supports clear actions.

Feature: List and inspect shared recipe library from offer workflow
User Story: As an offer operator, I can list and retrieve recipes used by the offer workflow.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Offer recipe endpoints require offer role and return shared RecipeLibrary items or 404 for unknown ids.

Feature: Import recipe text from offer workflow
User Story: As an offer operator, I can import recipe text into the shared recipe library.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: POST import-text parses uploaded recipe text, saves recipe, and logs source tier/approval state.

Feature: Upload recipe file from offer workflow
User Story: As an offer operator, I can upload a recipe file for extraction and library import.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Multipart upload validates metadata/limits, extracts document text, parses recipe, saves it, and returns upload errors on invalid files.

User Story: As an offer operator, I can approve, verify, or reject an imported recipe.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: PATCH review updates recipe approval state and logs review decision.

Feature: Normalize text or structured request to accepted spec
User Story: As an intake operator, I can turn a customer request into an AcceptedEventSpec.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: POST /v1/intake/normalize accepts EventRequest or text, stores request/spec, evaluates readiness, and logs normalization.

Feature: Create accepted spec from manual form
User Story: As an intake operator, I can enter event fields manually and create an accepted spec.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: POST /v1/intake/specs/manual builds EventRequest from form fields, normalizes to spec, stores request/spec, and audits.

Feature: Upload intake documents as JSON base64
User Story: As an intake operator, I can submit document content for ingestion and spec creation.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: POST /v1/intake/documents validates documents, ingests text, stores request/spec, returns ingestion summary, and audits.

Feature: Upload intake documents as multipart file
User Story: As an intake operator, I can directly upload PDF/email/text files into intake.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Multipart upload enforces limits/metadata validation, extracts documents, stores request/spec, and returns upload errors safely.

User Story: As an intake operator, I can list active requests and open a request detail.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: GET requests supports includeArchived query; detail returns request or 404.

User Story: As an intake operator, I can list active accepted specs and open a spec detail.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: GET specs supports includeArchived query; detail returns spec or 404.

Feature: Soft-archive wrong or stale intake context
User Story: As an operator, I can remove a wrong upload or rehearsal context from active focus without hard delete.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: POST archive validates reasonCode, archives request and related specs, returns archived spec ids, and logs no hard delete.

Feature: Edit accepted spec fields and components
User Story: As an operator, I can correct event date, attendees, service form, menu items, categories, production modes, purchase elements, and recipe overrides.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: PATCH /v1/intake/specs/:specId applies field and component updates, re-evaluates readiness, stores spec, and audits.
Primary Surface: UI production spec editor; PATCH spec endpoint

User Story: As an audit operator, I can record a governance finalize event for a spec or change set.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: POST finalize requires operations audit role, validates specId/changeSetId, logs finalize audit, and returns ok payload.

User Story: As a production operator, I can enter free text and create a production-ready spec through intake.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Production text action calls intake normalize and focuses returned accepted spec id.

Feature: Create production spec from manual form
User Story: As a production operator, I can create an accepted spec with structured fields from production route.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Manual form validates/submits fields through intake manual spec endpoint and focuses returned spec.

Feature: Upload source document with progress state
User Story: As a production operator, I can upload a source document and see loading/progress/success/failure state.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Document upload actions start progress, submit multipart document, complete with accepted spec id, or keep failed file retryable.

User Story: As a production operator, I can choose whether an upload is PDF, email, or text intake.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Document channel state exposes supported channel options and sends channel to intake upload.

User Story: As a production operator, I can drag a source file onto the production route.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Window file drop is scoped to production route, sets file draft, and tracks drag state.

Feature: Display upload limit and validation errors
User Story: As a production operator, I can see why an upload failed.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Upload errors are formatted from server response and kept visible in the workbench, including size/metadata validation failures.

User Story: As a production operator, I can search and narrow specs, plans, recipes, and audit context.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Search text filters dashboard records and route state keeps focused/current artifacts scoped.

User Story: As a production operator, I can switch between specs without stale questions or artifacts leaking.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Focus state chooses selected/search/current spec and resets stale intake detail, question state, and artifact context.

Feature: View intake origin and source metadata
User Story: As a production operator, I can see where the focused spec came from and whether ingestion had warnings.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Origin card resolves request detail, source lineage, filename, ingestion status, and warning summary.

Feature: Clear active workspace without deleting data
User Story: As a production operator, I can clear current workspace focus without deleting plans or lists.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Workspace reset clears selected focus/state, disables clear when no context exists, and leaves stored objects as archived/non-current context.

Feature: See open and answered clarification questions
User Story: As a production operator, I can see outstanding and answered clarification questions for a spec.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Question panel builds open/answered status, grouped conversation projection, and read-only anchors for answered items.

User Story: As a production operator, I can submit structured answers to open clarification questions.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Question actions build answer payloads, persist answers, update status, and prevent duplicate reopen while editor is open.

User Story: As a production operator, I can have the question editor open automatically when a spec needs answers.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Auto-open state is route-scoped and avoids reopening already focused/answered states.

Feature: Generate and review KI clarification drafts
User Story: As a production operator, I can generate draft clarification questions and approve or reject them before they become product questions.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Draft route builds schema-backed input, validates provider output, persists pending_review drafts, lists them, and approve materializes questions while reject does not.
Primary Surface: UI flag VITE_SHOW_LLM_DRAFTS; production draft endpoints

Feature: Edit event facts and menu items
User Story: As a production operator, I can edit event type/date/attendees/service form/menu items before planning.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Spec editor snapshots current spec, tracks dirty state, builds PATCH input, and persists updates.

Feature: Classify menu components and production mode
User Story: As a production operator, I can classify each menu component as classic/vegetarian/vegan and scratch/hybrid/purchase/external.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Component fields update component state and PATCH body with menuCategory, productionMode, purchasedElements, notes, and recipeOverrideId.

Feature: Assign specific recipe to a component
User Story: As a production operator, I can assign a known recipe override to a menu component.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Override select exposes recipe choices and stores recipeOverrideId on component update.

Feature: Create production plan and purchase list from accepted spec
User Story: As a production operator, I can start calculation and receive a production plan plus purchase list.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: POST /v1/production/plans validates spec, builds artifacts, saves plan/list, logs audit, and returns both artifacts.

Feature: Show planning progress and failure state
User Story: As a production operator, I can see that plan calculation is running, completed, or failed.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Planning progress state tracks phase, ETA, progress label, focused spec label, success, and failure messages.

User Story: As a production operator, I can see when a plan is fallback, blocked, or operationally incomplete.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Planning rules produce readiness, unresolved items, fallback reasons, warnings, and UI status surfaces avoid claiming completion.

User Story: As a production operator, I can get internal recipe matches for menu components.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Recipe discovery scores internal candidates by archetype/category/diet/ingredients and records recipe selections.

Feature: Use web recipe fallback when enabled
User Story: As a production operator, I can get reviewed web fallback candidates when internal recipes are missing and web search is enabled.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Web provider is disabled by default; env flag enables DuckDuckGo provider and web candidate materialization/quality checks.

Feature: Create procurement items for explicit purchased elements
User Story: As a production operator, I can mark components as purchased or hybrid and have procurement items appear in the purchase list.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Planning creates procurement artifacts for purchased elements/external finished items and keeps baker purchase branches explicit.

Feature: List and open production purchase lists
User Story: As a production operator, I can list purchase lists and open a specific list.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: GET purchase list endpoints return all lists or one list by id, with 404 for unknown id.

Feature: Preview current purchase list in UI
User Story: As a production operator, I can see key purchase list items, quantities, units, and recipe source labels.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Purchase preview supports canonical and legacy shapes, limits preview rows, and formats source metadata/fallbacks.

User Story: As a production operator, I can see when old purchase lists look polluted by recipe instructions.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Quality warning detects instruction-like article names, shows examples, and marks them as stale-data warnings.
Primary Surface: UI purchase list panel; local check

Feature: Sort purchasing items by Metro group order
User Story: As a production operator, I can receive purchase list items grouped in canonical Metro order.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Purchasing rules sort known Metro groups by canonical order, unknown groups last, and export group labels in German.

User Story: As a production operator, I can distinguish current plans/purchase lists from older or unrelated artifacts.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Artifact selection and object panel state scope current artifacts to focused spec/selected plan and label archived context separately.

User Story: As a production operator, I can inspect selected plan batches, kitchen sheets, recipe selections, unresolved items, and warnings.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Selected plan state and secondary details render plan context, spec context, and operational detail labels.

Feature: View recipe library and review status in production
User Story: As a production operator, I can see recipe count, approved/review-required status, and recipe controls.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Recipe panel state computes review counts and library panel renders status and recipe controls.

Feature: Import recipe text in production workflow
User Story: As a production operator, I can import recipe text into the production recipe repository.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: POST production import-text parses, saves, audits, and returns the recipe.

Feature: Upload recipe file in production workflow
User Story: As a production operator, I can upload a recipe file for extraction and import.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Multipart recipe upload validates file metadata/limits, extracts text, parses recipe, saves, and handles upload errors.

User Story: As a production operator, I can approve, verify, or reject recipes.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: PATCH production recipe review updates approval state, source tier, and audit log.

User Story: As a production operator, I can open a print-ready production plan export.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Export service requires production role, loads plan, returns HTML, and 404s unknown plans.

User Story: As a production operator, I can open a nine-section production folder with plan, spec, recipes, purchase list, timeline, and coverage.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Export resolves plan/spec/purchase lists/recipes/clarification answers, returns 404 for missing plan/spec, and renders honest empty-state notes.

User Story: As a production operator, I can download purchase list CSV for procurement.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Export service requires production role, loads purchase list, returns text/csv with canonical headers, and 404s unknown lists.

Feature: Enforce role gates on mutating routes
User Story: As the platform, mutating actions require the correct operator role.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Trusted actor headers/dev auth resolve minimal MVP role; unauthorized requests receive 403 on protected mutating routes.

User Story: As the platform, unsafe or oversized uploads are rejected before ingestion.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Upload security validates extension/MIME/size and returns bounded error messages for intake/recipe contexts.

User Story: As an audit operator, I can trace normalization, draft creation, planning, seeding, recipe review, and AI draft decisions.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Services write AuditLog entries with actor, action, entity, summary, and bounded details; audit endpoint lists recent production audit events.

Feature: Build BYO LLM adapter from env
User Story: As an operator, I can explicitly choose fixture, OpenAI, or Codex CLI provider for draft-only LLM use.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Runtime defaults to fixture, requires explicit OpenAI model/key for OpenAI, supports codex_cli via subprocess, and does not silently fall back.

User Story: As the platform, AI draft audit metadata must not store raw prompts or raw model responses.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Agent audit records contain ids/hashes/provider metadata but tests assert no prompt or response plaintext in audit.

User Story: As an operator, I can import verified Köpff recipe seeds into the recipe library without duplicate imports.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Import script loads 11 seed JSON recipes through upload/library logic with review-required status and idempotency.

User Story: As an operator, I can regenerate curated offer package fixture from source portfolio data.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Import script validates required package fields, strips marker lists, sorts by id, and writes curated-offer-packages.json idempotently.

Feature: Select Uni Rahmenvertrag packages and estimate side costs
User Story: As an operator, I can query Uni package options by event type/pax and estimate transport/staff side costs.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: selectUniPackages filters min_pax and event type substring; estimateUniSideCosts applies delivery bands and staff hourly rate.
Notes: No UI/API surface in current code evidence.

User Story: As an operator, I can run a local stack with seeded demo data and validate health/export/audit anchors.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: local:start, local:start:fresh, local:status, local:check, and local:stop manage screen sessions and bounded local verification.

User Story: As an operator, I can run scripted browser rehearsals for core UI flows.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Browser rehearsal scripts exercise non-mutating and controlled mutating/fresh flows for answer submit, archive intake, failed upload, and full fresh run.

Feature: Run LLM synthetic live and mini-pilot checks
User Story: As an operator, I can run preflight, probe, strict probe, and mini-pilot checks for synthetic LLM readiness.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: llm scripts validate env/fixtures, run guarded probes, fail on eval drift, and expose mini-pilot ready status for UI paste-in.

Feature: Use file storage or PostgreSQL-backed collection storage
User Story: As an operator, I can run services on default file storage or configure PostgreSQL database URL.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Stores accept rootDir/databaseUrl/pgPool options; README documents CATERING_DATA_ROOT and CATERING_DATABASE_URL.

User Story: As the platform, untrusted names/text must not render executable HTML in exports.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Export tests verify script-like recipe names and content are escaped rather than rendered raw.

Feature: Run one internal catering flow from intake to production artifacts
User Story: As an internal operator, I can enter a realistic request, produce a usable plan, and inspect purchase/export evidence.
Expected Behavior Based On Code: Backoffice smoke walks manual intake through accepted spec, production plan, purchase list, and exports with realistic data.
